To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the source size of the pions in the transverse plane is independent of the pion pair transverse momentum, and that the source size in the longitudinal plane is independent of centrality and the pair transverse momentum.

the pion HBT radii in Au+Au root(s)(NN)=200 GeV collisions are consistent with hydrodynamic model predictions and that the ratio of the HBT radii is consistent with 1, indicating that the pion source is approximately Gaussian.
the Bertsch- Pratt radius parameters are consistent with the predictions of hydrodynamical calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the space-time evolution of the hadronization process of the fireball produced in Au+Au heavy-ion collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC).
the study of the space-time structure of particle production in high energy nuclear collisions.
the study of Bose-Einstein correlations between charged pions in Au+Au reactions at root(NN)=200GeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the measured pion source size is consistent with the hydrodynamical predictions and the measured ratio R-out/Rside is also consistent with unity, which is expected from a source with no significant net electric charge.
, within the current precision of the measurements, the pion source is consistent with being a static source with a Gaussian profile.
the measured pion HBT radii are consistent with hydrodynamic flow and are not significantly influenced by the initial geometry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the measured Bertsch- Pratt radii are consistent with the predictions from the hydrodynamic model, and the ratio R-out/ R-side is consistent with unity within the limits of our knowledge of the Coulomb fraction.
the pion source at RHIC energies is consistent with a source which has a small longitudinal extent and which is approximately Gaussian in shape in relative momentum space.
we have shown that the Bertsch- Pratt radii determined by PHENIX for charged pion pairs from Au+Au collisions are in agreement with the results from other experiments and theoretical calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pion-pion radius parameter is constant at 0.2 GeV/c.
the Bertsch- Pratt radius parameters are consistent with those from lower-energy heavy-ion collisions.
the ratio R-out / R-side is constant with centrality and transverse momentum.
